title: Find Median from Data Stream: Two Groups at a Children's Party
summary: A max-heap holds the younger half and a min-heap the older half; their roots give the median at any moment.

analogy.scenario: Children arrive at a party one at a time, each telling their age. The host must always be able to name the middle age, so the host splits the children into a younger group and an older group of equal size.

mapping.real: The younger group, oldest of them in front
mapping.abstract: A max-heap of the lower half

mapping.real: The older group, youngest of them in front
mapping.abstract: A min-heap of the upper half
Rebalancing: pop one root, push it on the other heap

takeaway.summary: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and the upper half in a min-heap, sizes equal or the lower one bigger by one. The median is the lower root, or the average of both roots.
takeaway.timeComplexity: O(log n) per addNum, O(1) per findMedian
whenToUse: A running median or other middle value
Splitting a stream into a lower and an upper half

scenes.narration: Children arrive at a party one at a time, aged 6, 2, 9, and 1. After each arrival the host must name the middle age.
scenes.caption: Children arrive one by one: what's the middle age now?

scenes.narration: Lining everyone up by age after each arrival works, but most of the line never changes.
scenes.caption: Re-sorting everyone at each arrival repeats the work

scenes.narration: Instead, keep two groups. The younger group's oldest child stands in front, and the older group's youngest child stands in front. The first child, aged 6, joins the younger group.
scenes.caption: Two groups: younger (oldest in front), older (youngest in front)

scenes.narration: A 2 joins the younger group, which now has two children and the older group none. Its front child, 6, moves to the older group.
scenes.caption: The younger group got too big: its front child moves over

scenes.narration: With one child in each group, the middle age is halfway between the two front children: 2 plus 6 is 8, half of that is 4.
scenes.caption: Equal groups: the middle is the average of the two fronts

scenes.narration: A 9 arrives. It's older than the younger group's front child, 2, so it joins the older group.
scenes.caption: 9 is older than the younger group's front: it joins the older

scenes.narration: The older group is now bigger, so its front child, 6, moves back to the younger group. The younger group may hold the one extra child.
scenes.caption: Now the older group is bigger: 6 moves back

scenes.narration: A 1 joins the younger group, 6 moves across again, and the groups are even. The middle age is again 2 plus 6, halved: 4.
scenes.caption: After 1 arrives: the middle age is (2 + 6) / 2 = 4

scenes.narration: Ages are the stream, the younger group is a max-heap, and the older group a min-heap. Adding costs O(log n); the median is always at the two roots.
scenes.caption: Ages are numbers; the groups are a max-heap and a min-heap
